summary: Non-deterministic tool execution order & duplicate side-effects when mixing SDKs and streaming reconnects
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports duplicate side-effects (duplicate job creations and webhook posts) when a chat session uses a combination of the TypeScript SDK for client-side streaming and a backend Python service that invokes tools via function-calling. Impact: NovaMaps sees duplicate jobs billed and double webhook deliveries causing downstream processing failures and user confusion. Environment: Dedicated plan, prod us-west, heavy multiplexed traffic from mobile clients.

Observed behavior: During intermittent mobile network flaps customers reconnect the streaming TS SDK. On reconnect the conversation resumes, but NovaMaps sees repeated tool invocations (same external job created twice, second with 409 race but still triggers webhook). The duplicates are intermittent (10-15% of reconnects) and often correlate with short reconnect windows (500ms-5s).

Expected behavior: Retries/reconnects should not cause duplicate externally visible side-effects; SDK and platform should provide clear guidance to implement at-most-once or idempotent patterns for tool/function calls.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Start a streaming chat with TS SDK (client sends partial tokens).
2) Backend (Python) receives function_call events and synchronously creates an external job (POST to customer API) without idempotency key.
3) Simulate a short network interruption and reconnect the TS stream; allow SDK to resume and resend buffered tokens.
4) Observe backend receiving what appears to be a replay or duplicate function_call and creating the external job a second time.
5) Repeat across multiplexed client connections to increase probability of race. Expected: single job created per logical user prompt. Observed: duplicates in ~1/8 attempts.
investigation_notes:
Initial logs show two function_call events with identical arguments separated by ~300-1200ms. The serving-runtime trace indicates both requests were routed to different worker shards (continuous batching enabled) and the second arrived after a short reconnect window. There is evidence of client-side buffered token replay: the TS SDK reopened the stream and replayed unacknowledged tokens. Python handler is synchronous and returns 200 quickly after creating job; no idempotency key used.

Hypothesis A: Client-side resume combined with lack of idempotency at the application layer allows duplicate tool side-effects.
Hypothesis B: Multiplexed batching + shard routing can reorder or duplicate function_call envelopes when SDK reconnection overlaps with prior in-flight request merge.

We reproduced locally by forcing a websocket close at the client after sending the function_call start token then reconnecting; backend saw two function_call webhooks. Enabling request logs on the serving runtime shows two separate request IDs but identical payloads.

Relevant traces and logs: link to internal trace: https://trace.redwood.ai/trace/abcd-190001; backend logs (redacted) show two POSTs to customer endpoint 2026-03-09T18:12:03Z and 2026-03-09T18:12:04Z.
comments: Support (Maya Patel) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged receipt; requested sample client/handler code and approximate timestamps. Asked for a short repro repro script.
Customer (NovaMaps - Rafael Ortiz) 2026-03-10: Provided minimal repro (TS client + Python webhook handler) and sample webhook URL. Noted duplicates correlate with cell-network reconnections.
SRE (Evan Liu) 2026-03-11: Confirmed duplicates in traces. No platform-level 'exactly-once' offered; recommended idempotency keys at handler. Asked Eng if SDK should expose sequence-nonce helper.

Eng (Anika Shah) 2026-03-12: Noted that continuous batching and shard routing can cause same logical message to be processed twice if clients replay unacknowledged buffers. Suggested pattern: include client-generated idempotency token + sequence number on function_call metadata and server-side dedup map with TTL.

Support (Maya Patel) 2026-03-13: Shared a mitigation guide and a small code sample for generating per-invocation idempotency tokens from client-provided conversation_id + function_call_nonce. Customer testing scheduled for 2026-03-14.
resolution:
Workaround provided: 1) Add a per-function-call idempotency token (UUIDv4) passed in function_call.metadata or top-level input metadata from the client. Backend must use that token when creating external jobs and perform a get-or-create (upsert) using the token as unique key. 2) For streaming resumes, SDK will be configured (client-side) to assign a monotonically increasing sequence number per partial function_call and attach the last-acked seq in resume messages. 3) Short-term recommended server fix: dedup table with 30s TTL keyed by idempotency token + customer id.

Long-term items: INT task to add optional SDK helper to auto-generate and attach idempotency tokens on function_call events (INT-4021). Engineering to evaluate providing explicit 'function_call_ack' event from runtime so clients can safely garbage collect buffered tokens (related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1198).
next_steps:
- Customer to test provided workaround and report results by 2026-03-14.
- INT-4021: Engineer owner assigned to evaluate SDK helper (ETA 2 sprints).
- Track related follow-ups in linked issues and update this ticket when SDK change PR is available.
final_status_notes: Open: customer testing in progress; workaround accepted pending results. Engineering follow-up tracked via INT-4021 and serving-runtime PR.
